Implements brief 005 (`docs/briefs/active.md` on `meta/round-2-close` at `3a2fea97`, PR #20). All four C++ modules (`client/`, `data/`, `policy/`, `ui/`) now configure, build under `-DEDOPRO_NEXT_WERROR=ON`, and pass `ctest` on Windows/MSVC — three focused fixes, one per defect, plus documentation for two operational gotchas the brief flagged as costing real time.

## Required investigation 1 — the one the brief cared about most

**No, production code does not carry the narrowing-conversion pattern.** Confirmed by building all four modules — `client/src`, `data/src`, `policy/src`, and `ui/src` — under `/W4 /WX` with MSVC 19.44.35228. The only narrowing warnings anywhere in any of the four builds were in `client/tests/test_protocol_decoder.cpp` (defect 1, fixed below). Every production `.cpp` across all four modules compiled with zero warnings under the same flags. This isn't a claim from reading the code — it's what actually happened when everything was built with `/WX` turned on.

## The three fixes

1. **`client/tests/test_protocol_decoder.cpp`** — narrower than the brief's own description: not just the two `proto::LOCATION_*` call sites, but every one of six `std::tuple<uint32_t, uint8_t, uint8_t, uint32_t>` literals, because MSVC also flags the bare `0` literal used for `controller` in each one — `std::tuple`'s variadic constructor forwards through a template parameter deduced as `int`, which doesn't get the "constant literal that fits" exemption ordinary scalar init gets. Fixed with a small typed helper (`confirm_cards_entry()`) rather than a wall of `static_cast`s — every element it assigns already matches the tuple's element type, so there's no narrowing left to silence.
2. **`data/CMakeLists.txt`** — `bench_card_search`'s `/O2` collides with the Debug configure's `/RTC1` (`D8016`, a hard error). The "obvious" fix — save/strip/restore `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG` around one `add_executable()` call — does **not** work; confirmed by testing it. CMake resolves a directory's flags variable once per directory at generate time, not per-target at the call site. The actual fix needed a directory boundary: moved `bench_card_search` into its own `data/tests/bench/CMakeLists.txt`. No other target's flags changed.
3. **`ui/tests/CMakeLists.txt`** — `test_deckbuilder_screen`'s QML files are shared with `edopro_next_shell` and referenced via `../qml/...`; Qt's qmlcachegen embeds that literal `..` into a cache-directory `mkdir()` call, which Windows rejects outright. The "obvious" fix — register the QML module from `ui/`'s own directory, where the real files already live with no `..` needed — **broke `edopro_next_shell` itself at runtime** (`Module "EdoproNext" contains no type named "Main"`), confirmed reproducible and confirmed absent immediately before that change. Discarded entirely rather than shipped as a partial fix. The fix that stayed: mirror the five shared files into `ui/tests/.qml_mirror/` at configure time (symlink with a staleness-checked copy fallback) and point `QML_FILES` at the mirror instead — no directory-scope change, no `..` anywhere.

## Two operational facts, documented in `AGENTS.md`'s evidence table itself

vcvars64.bat is required for `cmake -G Ninja` to find a compiler at all; `data/`/`policy/`/`ui/` need the vcpkg toolchain file and triplet, `ui/` additionally needs Qt's `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`; Qt's `bin/` needs to be on `PATH` at `ctest` runtime or it reports `BAD_COMMAND` (reads as a build failure, isn't one). Also recorded, per the brief's own instruction not to chase them: a one-off spurious `BAD_COMMAND` right after a parallel link (Windows file-locking, passes on re-run), and a freshly-linked `.exe` blocked once by a local Application Control policy on first launch (cleared by deleting and relinking, seen on two unrelated executables).
